ai.description: Eutropis gansi reaches a snout-vent length of 7–8 cm. It is bronze-brown with a dark lateral stripe and a pale venter. It is distinguished by three keeled dorsal scales and smooth subdigital lamellae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Eutropis gansi* is best distinguished by its distinct lack of a supranasal scale, a feature that separates it from most other Indian *Eutropis* species.
ai.habitat: Gans' Mabuya inhabits the moist deciduous forests and scrublands of the Western Ghats, typically found at low to moderate elevations within leaf litter and rocky outcrops.
ai.behavior: Eutropis gansi is a diurnal lizard that actively hunts for small insects and invertebrates among leaf litter and low-lying vegetation during the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Eutropis gansi* is viviparous, producing a litter of 3–6 young. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Eutropis gansi* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
